approved: Water Efficiency Labelling and Standards Amendment (Registration Fees) Bill 2013
Sustainability, Environment, Water, Population and Communities

Introduced the Water Efficiency Labelling and Standards Amendment Registration Fees Bill, making consequential changes to allow proper collection and administration of the new registration fees introduced by the companion bill.
Moved to refer the Water Efficiency Labelling and Standards (Registration Fees) Bill and its amendment bill to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

Supported the WELS registration fees bills, arguing that labelling helps consumers choose efficient products and could save about 100,000 megalitres of domestic water use each year by 2025, 800,000 megalitres nationally and about 400,000 tonnes of greenhouse gas emissions each year. Said compliance should protect the system's integrity while being applied with common sense.
Reported that the WELS registration fees bills provide for the scheme's long-term viability and supported the scheme's contribution to water efficiency in Australia. Commended the bills to the House.
Water Efficiency Labelling and Standards Amendment (Registration Fees) Act 2013
